transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2027-06-11
Start: 16:00 UTC
Duration: ~58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Carlos Ruiz (Redwood SE), Dr. Lena Park (Equinox, CTO), Rahul Singh (Head of Infra), Marta Lopez (Security Architect)

Auto-summary (auto-generated, may be incomplete): Kickoff to scope POC for private networking and residency. Discussed VPC peering vs PrivateLink, region lock requirements (eu-west-1), egress constraints (no egress to third-party subnets), baseline perf targets (p95 < 150ms for short prompts, 50 reqs/sec sustained for T4 cluster equivalence), and next steps to share diagrams, runbook, and benchmark harness.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood): Hey everyone, thanks for making time. Quick roll call, we'll keep this tight 45-60, objective is to walk POC scope and agree acceptance criteria.
[00:18] Dr. Lena Park (Equinox): Hi, Lena here. Thanks. We're looking to validate private deployment patterns and perf for our internal genomics pipeline.
[00:28] Rahul: Rahul here, infra. We'll handle VPC side.
[00:31] Marta: Marta, security. I'll be tracking compliance asks.
[00:34] Carlos (Redwood): Carlos here, SE. I'll own benchmarks and runbook.
[00:38] Maya: Cool. Quick agenda — connectivity options, residency constraints, benchmark plan, and success metrics + timeline. Anything to add?
[00:47] Dr. Lena: No, that's good.
[00:49] Rahul: One ask — we need zero egress to outside eu-west-1; also can't open broad internet egress from the hosting subnet.
[00:58] Maya: Got it. We'll treat region lock as firm. We'll also map PrivateLink vs peering trade-offs.
[01:05] Carlos: If I can jump in — operationally peering is simpler but requires route table changes and cross-account peering; PrivateLink keeps traffic inside AWS backbone and uses ENIs, but introduces NLBs and can be trickier for large payloads. Also cost profiles differ.
[01:28] Marta: Can you explain attack surface differences? Is PrivateLink more secure because it uses interface endpoints?
[01:34] Carlos: Generally yes, but misconfig can expose NLB. Peering is more transparent but you need strict route table + NACL controls. Also with peering, DNS resolution requires extra setup (resolver rules) if you need private DNS.
[01:49] Dr. Lena: We prefer minimal changes to our infra team — peering might be less ops up front, but if PrivateLink reduces attack surface that's valuable.
[02:00] Rahul: Our infra team doesn't want cross-account roles if possible. We prefer VPC peering but only if there's no egress to public net.
[02:09] Maya: Noted. We'll propose both diagrams.
[02:12] Carlos: On benchmarks: want to confirm workload profile. Lena, can you describe typical prompts and expected token lengths?
[02:21] Dr. Lena: Sure — two main patterns: short clinical prompts (50-150 tokens) for triage and longer sequence analysis (1.5k - 3k tokens) for batch summarization. We expect peak burstiness from UI of ~200 RPS for short prompts but sustained load maybe 20-30 RPS; the long sequences are lower rps but heavy tokens.
[02:47] Maya: Great — so we'll plan two load profiles: Short prompt burst (200 RPS for 60s windows), sustained short prompt (30 RPS for 10m), and long sequence batch (5-10 RPS with 2-3k tokens).
[03:05] Carlos: We'll determine target latency SLOs. Typical ask is p95 < 150ms for short prompts with streaming disabled; for long sequences we'll optimize for throughput and p95 maybe < 2s depending on model/quantization.
[03:22] Marta: Are you talking about hosted or Private? We need to make sure no tokens leave the region — KMS usage too.
[03:29] Carlos: This is Redwood Private inside your VPC; logs and KV cache remain in-region. KMS can be customer-managed; we'll integrate with your AWS KMS CMKs.
[03:39] Rahul: KMS must be in our account. No shared key across Redwood.
[03:42] Maya: That's supported — typical pattern is customer-owned CMK and key policies we've used before. We'll include that in the SOC/PK.
[03:50] Dr. Lena: On metrics: we want to see token-level cost breakdown, latency percentiles, and per-route SLOs in the console.
[03:59] Maya: Yes we'll produce a dashboard template for the POC with token breakdown, per-model latency histograms, error rates.
[04:07] Carlos: Benchmark notes — we'll run three passes: cold start (no KV cache, fresh model), warmed run (with KV cache primed), and production-ish run with prefix caching. We'll also test quantized model variant to compare cost/latency trade-offs.
[04:24] Rahul: How do you simulate our traffic? Do you need a dataset?
[04:27] Carlos: Ideally a synthetic harness from your sample prompts + a small corpus of long docs to emulate summarization. If you can't share PII, obfuscated samples are fine.
[04:36] Dr. Lena: We'll provide anonymized samples.
[04:39] Marta: On compliance — we need audit logs, access control, and retention policies. Can logs be sent to our CloudWatch/ELK?
[04:46] Maya: Yes logs can be pushed to your account; we can stream audit logs into CloudWatch or S3. Retention policies are configurable.
[04:53] Marta: Also SSO — we use Okta, SAML-based.
[04:56] Carlos: Redwood supports SAML SSO and role-based access. We'll give a checklist for SAML integration.
[05:03] Dr. Lena: What's the timeline? We need results before the end of Q3.
[05:07] Maya: For a 4-week POC we can start stack week of 6/21, run bench runs week of 6/28 and deliver report by 7/19 — that fits Q3, margin to extend if needed.
[05:18] Rahul: Week of 6/21 is fine as long as we have the network diagrams and a minimal runbook by 6/16 to prep.
[05:25] Maya: We'll aim to deliver diagrams & SOW by 6/14, runbook by 6/16 as action items.
[05:31] Carlos: A few technical clarifications — do you expect persistent KV cache pinned across sessions? For genomics batch we may want a warmed key cache between steps.
[05:41] Dr. Lena: Yes we expect long-running sessions for some workflows; cache persistence is important.
[05:45] Carlos: Ok we'll include a KV cache strategy; note that cache hits can drop per-token cost substantially. We'll quantify that in the benchmarking.
[05:55] Maya: Any blockers from compliance side?
[05:58] Marta: We need a short questionnaire: encryption at rest, in transit, key ownership, access logs, PCA/pen test attestation. I'll send the list.
[06:07] Maya: Great — action item for Marta to send list by 6/15.
[06:10] Rahul: On connectivity — we have an existing transit VPC. Will peering require a route through transit? We prefer not to create new transits.
[06:19] Carlos: We can do either: peer directly to a dedicated Redwood VPC or use PrivateLink endpoints attached into your transit. We'll diagram both so you can evaluate. Peering may need route propagation in transit.
[06:31] Dr. Lena: Can you talk about egress controls? We need assurance that model downloads, telemetry, or other control plane operations don't cause data to leave region.
[06:40] Carlos: In Redwood Private, model artifacts can be pre-provisioned in-region. Control plane calls (for updates) can be gated; we'll run the deployment with no outbound internet egress except to approved S3 endpoints and our management plane over a controlled connection. We'll include an egress CIDR allowlist.
[06:58] Marta: So we need a signed doc that states no telemetry will be sent to outside vendors without permission.
[07:04] Maya: We'll include a binding statement in the SOW and we have GDPR + SOC2 addenda we can attach.
[07:09] Rahul: For benchmarking hardware — are we testing on T4s or A100s? Cost difference is big.
[07:15] Carlos: For POC we'll test on two configs: a cost-oriented setup (T4 equivalent) and a high-perf setup (A100 or similar). We'll show cost per 1k tokens and latency profiles.
[07:28] Dr. Lena: We care about latency for the UI use-case — p95 < 200ms would be ideal, but we'll take p95 < 300ms as acceptable.
[07:36] Maya: Let's capture that as acceptance: UI short prompts p95 < 300ms (goal < 200ms). Long sequences p95 < 2s. Cost target TBD but we'll show delta.
[07:46] Carlos: Also we'll include failure/fallback behavior: if primary model is constrained we'll show a smaller model fallback to maintain latency SLOs.
[07:56] Dr. Lena: Good to have graceful degradation.
[07:59] Maya: Next, benchmarks specifics — Carlos, walk through proposed tests.
[08:03] Carlos: Test matrix: Model variants (full precision, 8-bit quantized), cache states (cold, warm), workloads (short burst, sustained, long batch), connectivity (peering vs PrivateLink, both to measure latency). We'll instrument with OpenTelemetry traces and provide raw traces + aggregated metrics.
[08:24] Rahul: How long do runs take? If we do three passes per variant it could take a day per variant.
[08:29] Carlos: We'll parallelize where possible; baseline runs should take 1-2 hours per config. Full matrix across two model variants and three cache states about 6-8 hours. We'll schedule windows with your infra.
[08:43] Marta: We need to ensure test data does not contain PHI; will you accept redacted datasets?
[08:48] Carlos: Absolutely, redacted/anonymized samples are standard. We'll provide a small harness for local validation first.
[08:55] Dr. Lena: On cost — will we get an estimate of projected monthly cost at production loads?
[09:00] Maya: We'll deliver a cost model: cost per 1M tokens and an extrapolation for your expected usage profiles. That's part of the POC report.
[09:08] Rahul: One more network detail — MTU and packet path. We had issues in the past with tunnel overhead causing fragmentation.
[09:15] Carlos: We'll validate MTU in the runbook. PrivateLink avoids some of that because it uses ENIs; peering will be through your VPC with standard MTU. We'll test for fragmentation.
[09:26] Maya: Any other questions before we move to wrap?
[09:29] Marta: Do you provide per-token logging? We only want aggregate usage logs, not raw prompts stored.
[09:35] Carlos: Default is aggregate; raw prompts can be configured — by default Redwood does not retain raw prompt content in longer-term logs unless customer opts in. We'll include a retention config in the SOW.
[09:48] Dr. Lena: Good. About rollback/rollouts: if a model update regresses quality how do you handle that?
[09:54] Carlos: We support pinned versions and can rollback to previous model versions. For POC we'll lock model version unless you request an upgrade. We also provide A/B and canary deploys for evaluation.
[10:05] Maya: Ok let's recap and assign owners. Recap: Redwood to send SOW + network diagrams (peering & PrivateLink) by 6/14; Carlos to share benchmark harness & runbook by 6/16; Equinox to send anonymized sample prompts and egress CIDR by 6/13; Marta to send compliance question list by 6/15. POC target start week of 6/21, first baseline runs week of 6/28, final report around 7/19.
[10:35] Rahul: Sounds good.
[10:37] Dr. Lena: One small ask — can Redwood also include a quick price delta for dedicated vs shared infra?
[10:43] Maya: Yes we'll include cost comparison in the SOW.
[10:45] Marta: Also include the KMS integration diagram and SAML checklist.
[10:48] Maya: Noted.
[10:50] Carlos: I'll also add a short checklist for PrivateLink NLB config and peering route examples.
[10:56] Maya: Anything else?
[10:58] Dr. Lena: No that's it. Thanks team.
[11:01] Maya: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with artifacts.
[11:04] (meeting ends)
